hints: Integrate by parts with u=x² and dv=sin2x dx.
Apply integration by parts again to the remaining x cos2x term, checking chain-rule factors.
Evaluate the complete primitive at 0 and π/6 using exact sine and cosine values.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts $\int u\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x = uv - \int v\dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\,\mathrm{d}x$ with:
$$u = x^2 \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = 2x$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = \sin(2x) \implies v = -\dfrac{1}{2}\cos(2x)$$
$$\int x^2\sin(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\cos(2x) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\cos(2x)\right)(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\cos(2x) + \int x\cos(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Apply integration by parts a second time to $\int x\cos(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x$ with:
$$u = x \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = \cos(2x) \implies v = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2x)$$
$$\int x\cos(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x\sin(2x) - \int \dfrac{1}{2}\sin(2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}x\sin(2x) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\cos(2x)\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}x\sin(2x) + \dfrac{1}{4}\cos(2x)$$

Combine the terms to obtain the complete antiderivative $F(x)$:
$$F(x) = -\dfrac{1}{2}x^2\cos(2x) + \dfrac{1}{2}x\sin(2x) + \dfrac{1}{4}\cos(2x)$$

Evaluate $F(x)$ at the upper limit $x = \dfrac{1}{6}\pi$ where $2x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}, \quad \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$
$$F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)^2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$$
$$= -\dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{\pi^2}{36}\right) + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{24} + \dfrac{1}{8} = -\dfrac{\pi^2}{144} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{24} + \dfrac{1}{8}$$

Subtract $F(0)$ from $F(\pi/6)$ to obtain the final exact value:
$$F\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) - F(0) = -\dfrac{\pi^2}{144} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{24} + \dfrac{1}{8} - \dfrac{2}{8} = -\dfrac{\pi^2}{144} + \dfrac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{24} - \dfrac{1}{8}$$

ai_rubric.Integration by Parts: Integration by parts gives $Ax^2\cos2x-\int Bx\cos2x\,dx$. Derives $-\dfrac12x^2\cos2x+\dfrac12x\sin2x+\dfrac14\cos2x$. The final result is $-\dfrac{\pi^2}{144}+\dfrac{\sqrt3\pi}{24}-\dfrac18$.
